claims.text: A .NET 10 microservices reference e-commerce platform with twelve bounded contexts, deliberately different architectural styles, shared building blocks, integration events, transactional outbox messaging, and local .NET Aspire orchestration.
Portfolio reference repository for contributors and maintainers working with twelve bounded contexts, architecture patterns, backend services, infrastructure, deployment, and documentation.
FreshCart backend platform: twelve bounded contexts behind a YARP gateway, with an Angular 20 companion storefront.
Identity, Catalog, Pricing, Basket, Ordering, Inventory, Payment, Delivery, Notification, CustomerSupport, Reviews, and Reporting use distinct architectural styles and persistence choices.
The edge gateway provides the browser trust boundary, reverse proxy routing, and cookie-to-JWT BFF exchange for downstream services.
Reporting provides executive KPI dashboards, QuestPDF invoices, ClosedXML Excel exports, scheduled Azure Blob reports, and event projections into MySQL.
Basket and Ordering use a transactional outbox with background publishing, while consumers use inbox-based idempotency for cross-service events.
The Aspire AppHost boots backing services, every microservice, and the gateway in one developer command for local development.
Shared service defaults configure OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and logs, plus service discovery, HttpClient resilience, and default health-check endpoints.
Cookie-first for browsers, JWT for everything else

FC

FreshCart Architecture Guide

Online Supermarket — .NET 10 + Angular 20 + Azure AKS

FreshCart — production-grade online supermarket platform

Twelve bounded contexts. Each implemented in a different architectural style on purpose, so the repository is a teaching artifact that demonstrates every pattern, every cross-cutting concern, and every Azure capability that a Senior / Tech Lead / Architect interview would ask about — anchored to running code, not slides.

Try it now — live demo + seeded credentials

The platform ships with three pre-seeded accounts so you can open the storefront, sign in, and walk through the customer + back-office flows in under a minute. Demo data is seeded automatically on first boot in the Development environment via IdentityDataSeeder.

Quick start — local (Aspire + Docker)

# 1. Backing services (SQL, Postgres, MySQL, Mongo, Redis, RabbitMQ, Seq, Grafana, Prometheus)
docker compose -f deploy/docker/docker-compose.yaml up -d

# 2. Whole stack via .NET Aspire — boots every microservice + seeds the demo accounts
dotnet run --project src/AspireAppHost/FreshCart.AppHost

# 3. Customer SPA (separate repo: github.com/amasen02/freshcart-web)
git clone https://github.com/amasen02/freshcart-web.git
cd freshcart-web && npm install && npm start

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Local backing-services stack for FreshCart.
# Brings up every database, cache, broker and observability tool that the
# microservices depend on so a developer can boot the whole platform with a
# single `docker compose up -d`.
#
# Service code itself is NOT started here — use `dotnet run` against the
# Aspire AppHost (src/AspireAppHost/FreshCart.AppHost) once this stack is up.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

name: freshcart-local

services:

  # --- Relational stores -------------------------------------------------------

  sqlserver:
    image: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest
    container_name: freshcart-sqlserver
    environment:
      ACCEPT_EULA: "Y"
